name: Frostbitten-Shrine
specific_features: Ruined alien structure preserved perfectly in the ice at the south pole
Methane frost crystals that form shrine-like arched formations
description: Frostbitten-Shrine is a small ice world at the outer reaches of its system, its surface a mosaic of carbon dioxide ice, methane frost, and water ice in varying proportions that create a subtly colored landscape of whites, pale blues, and faint pinks. The methane frost crystallizes in the low gravity into arched formations that span meters, their translucent structures catching ambient starlight and refracting it into faint spectral displays. The thin atmosphere is barely detectable, a vestigial envelope of nitrogen and trace gases insufficient to support any known form of life.

The cold here is among the most extreme of any surveyed solid body, temperatures dipping low enough to freeze gases that remain vaporous on most ice worlds. The methane arches are fragile, a careless approach generating enough thermal radiation to sublimate their delicate crystal structures. Movement on the surface requires exquisite care, the frost formations beautiful and irreplaceable in their natural configuration, each one a unique product of conditions that took centuries to produce.

The south polar region holds Frostbitten-Shrine's most significant discovery: the ruins of an alien structure, partially exposed by cryogenic erosion and preserved by the extreme cold in a state of remarkable integrity. The structure's architecture does not match any known civilization's building patterns, its curved walls and sealed chambers suggesting a function that has not been determined. The materials resist analysis, returning ambiguous results that suggest either extreme age or an origin outside the known material science of any documented species. Carbon dating of organic traces within the structure indicates an age of at least two billion years.

The alien ruins have been classified at the highest archaeological priority level, with a permanent research station established in orbit to coordinate study. Surface access is restricted to teams that have demonstrated the ability to operate without thermally contaminating the site, as even body heat can damage the frost formations and potentially alter the preservation conditions that have kept the structure intact for eons. The methane and carbon dioxide ice deposits are commercially valuable but extraction has been prohibited within the south polar exclusion zone, extending the protection to the entire hemisphere as a precaution against subsurface disruption of the ruins.
